chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it, said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no goodness in neglecting the Hajj'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on neglecting the obligatory Hajj in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the absence of Hajj is not a neutral state of 'goodness' but rather a deficiency, emphasizing the obligatory nature of the pilgrimage for those who are able. This reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that neglecting Hajj without a valid excuse (like illness or poverty) constitutes a sin, as the command in the Quran is imperative. The narration underscores that the duty is binding and its omission is a spiritual loss rather than a voluntary merit.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, raising it,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no goodness in neglecting the Hajj’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that there is nothing of goodness in neglecting al-Hajj.”
